newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Official wants to launder Colombia's image.
newsitem.headline: Official wants to launder Colombia's image.

text.p: Communications Minister Saulo Arboleda called on Sunday for a wholesale laundering of Colombia's image, insisting that the country was a marvellous one, not a haven for drugs and violence.

"We must show the world that the reality in Colombia is not just violence and drug trafficking, as, falsely and unfortunately, foreigners believe," he said at the opening of an international conference against violence in the Caribbean port of Cartagena.

Arboleda's upbeat comments went hand in hand with a call for media self-censorship to tone down negative images of a country that has the highest kidnap rate in the world and Latin America's oldest and largest leftist guerrilla movement. Colombia's cartels also provide an estimated 80 percent of the world's cocaine and the majority of the heroin in the United States.

The communications chief singled out Nobel laureate Gabriel Garcia Marquez as one of the positive images of Colombia. Garcia Marquez's latest bestseller centres on the wave of kidnappings and terror attacks unleashed by the late drug lord Pablo Escobar in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
